Subject: Proposal — bucketed annual prepay structure

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the time earlier. Attached is a short summary of what CrestPoint is hoping to agree to: we want to prepay for capacity but frontload value into year 1 to support our ramp (Q1 is heavy with model training). High level ask: a 3-year term with annual prepay but with a bucket that lets us shift up to 25% of year 1 capacity into year 2 if we underspend.

Can Redwood do a structured discount that is higher in year 1 (to help with cashflow and training costs) and steps down in years 2–3, while preserving an overall minimum committed spend?

I've attached our usage forecast and a simple table of the frontload we're thinking.

Attachments: CrestPoint_Usage_Forecast.xlsx

Cheers,

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>

Cc:

Subject: Re: Proposal — bucketed annual prepay structure

Olga / Neha — read and ran the numbers against CP's forecast. I suggest we present two alternative structures so CrestPoint can choose by appetite for up-front cash vs long-term unit economics.

Option A (Frontloaded):
- 3-year term, annual prepay each year
- Year1 discount: 20% off list token rate (applied to the prepay bucket)
- Year2: 12%
- Year3: 8%
- Carryover: up to 25% of unused Year1 bucket into Year2 only; any unused in Year2 expires
- Payment: Year1 upfront (net 30), Year2/Year3 invoiced annually with credit for remaining bucket

Option B (Smoothed):
- 3-year term, annual prepay
- Year1: 15%
- Year2: 11%
- Year3: 10%
- Carryover: bidirectional within 12-month windows but capped aggregate at 15% of committed

Risks / approvals: anything >18% in year1 needs Sales Director approval (commercial policy), and >20% needs Rev Ops + Finance Exec approval. If Olga wants, I can ask for an exception for 20% to help win this given CP's strategic pipeline.

I attached a short PDF with the modeled impact to unit cost and to Redwood revenue recognition.

-Vivek

Thanks Vivek — the models look reasonable. A few finance asks before we send to customer:

- For the 20% Year1 ask: Finance prefers to cap at 18% unless sales gets a Director exception. If we push 20% we need a mandate (strategic value doc) and a shortened escalation path for approval.

Sara — good news: Redwood can accept a frontloaded Option A with a negotiated tweak. Summary we can offer:
- 3-year term, annual prepay
- Year1: 18% off list (we agreed to 18% to stay within Finance guardrails)
- Year2: 12%
- Year3: 8%
- Carryover: up to 20% of unused Year1 bucket into Year2 (one-way), documented reporting monthly
- Payment: Year1 upfront (net 30), Year2/Year3 invoiced annually with credits applied for carryover usage
